boards.school_name: University of North Carolina School of the Arts
boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented UNCSA spaces for reading, research, group work, score study, and project preparation.

cards.title: Library and Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: UNCSA campus
cards.notes: Start at the main desk, then choose a workspace for reading or a project meeting. Ask library staff which areas fit your task.
cards.short_summary: The campus library’s central study and collaboration setting.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s library describes its Library and Learning Commons spaces as available for study, collaboration, and instruction.
cards.access_notes: Library space reservations are offered through UNCSA’s library resources; confirm the space’s current booking rules before arriving.

cards.title: First-Floor Browsing Area
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons
cards.notes: Use this browsing area when current magazines or visual reference are part of the assignment; gather materials before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A library area beside the latest magazine issues.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA Library states that latest magazine issues are in the first-floor browsing area behind the stairs.
cards.access_notes: Use library materials according to current library policies; ask staff for help locating periodicals.

cards.title: Second-Floor Magazine Collection
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons
cards.notes: Bring a topic or visual brief and browse the physical magazine collection for reference material, then record useful citations or images.
cards.short_summary: A library-floor destination for physical magazine research.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA Library identifies the second floor as the location for most physical magazine material.
cards.access_notes: Library access and collection use are subject to current library policies.

cards.title: Third-Floor Music Books
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons
cards.notes: Use the third-floor ML and MT shelves for music research; pair a call number with a focused reading or score-analysis session.
cards.short_summary: A collection-based study stop for music books.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA Library says music books with ML and MT call numbers are on the library’s third floor.
cards.access_notes: Ask the Music Help Desk or library staff for collection assistance and current access guidance.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Score Collection
cards.subtitle: Library and Learning Commons
cards.notes: Take a course-specific composer, work, or ensemble size to the fourth floor and use the physical score and recording collections.
cards.short_summary: A music-focused floor with scores, recordings, and periodicals.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA Library lists sheet music, music reference works, scores, bound periodicals, CDs, DVDs, and LPs on its fourth floor.
cards.access_notes: Ask at the Music Help Desk for assistance with mini scores and audio or video recordings.

cards.title: UNCSA Archives Research Room
cards.subtitle: Third floor, University Library Annex
cards.notes: Book an appointment with the archives for primary-source research. Bring a laptop or pencil and paper, and follow the handling guidelines.
cards.short_summary: An appointment-based room for studying UNCSA archival materials.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA Archives is open for research by appointment and permits laptops, phones, pencils, and paper for note-taking in its Research Room.
cards.source_title: Using the Research Room — UNCSA Archives
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, staff, and the public by appointment; access is via the third-floor bridge from the main library.

cards.title: Artist Village Floor Studies
cards.subtitle: Artist Village residence hall
cards.notes: If you live in Artist Village, use the study on your floor for a focused work block; keep shared residential-space expectations in mind.
cards.short_summary: Residential study rooms distributed across Artist Village floors.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA states that Artist Village has studies on each floor.
cards.access_notes: This is a residence-hall amenity; access is governed by current Housing policies and resident access.

cards.entity_name: Semans Arts and Administration Building Seminar Rooms
cards.title: SAAB Seminar Rooms
cards.subtitle: Semans Arts and Administration Building
cards.notes: Use a seminar room only when it is scheduled or available for your academic activity; check the current campus reservation process first.
cards.short_summary: Seminar rooms in UNCSA’s renovated former library building.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA reports that the Semans Arts and Administration Building includes seminar rooms for students.
cards.source_title: Walk through the renovated Semans Arts & Administration Building — UNCSA
cards.access_notes: Confirm room availability and any required approval through the current UNCSA campus reservation process.

cards.entity_name: Semans Arts and Administration Building Practice Rooms
cards.title: SAAB Practice Rooms
cards.subtitle: Semans Arts and Administration Building
cards.notes: For individual preparation, verify whether a practice room is available and follow the building’s current scheduling and use expectations.
cards.short_summary: Practice rooms within the renovated Semans arts building.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA reports that the Semans Arts and Administration Building includes practice rooms where students can create and share work.
cards.source_title: Reinventing the spaces where we create and share our work — UNCSA
cards.access_notes: Room use is subject to current building access and scheduling requirements.

cards.title: Yekovich Conference Room
cards.subtitle: School of Music Complex
cards.notes: For a scheduled group session, coordinate with the School of Music and use the room for discussion, planning, or collaborative coursework.
cards.short_summary: A named conference room in the School of Music Complex.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCSA’s campus map lists the Yekovich Conference Room in the School of Music Complex, and its reservation directory names the School of Music contact for the room.
cards.source_title: Who to Contact to Reserve Campus Space — UNCSA
cards.access_notes: Coordinate through the School of Music; UNCSA lists it as the reserving office for the Yekovich Conference Room.
